description: JuPedSim is an open-source library for simulating pedestrian dynamics: individual agents walk through a polygonal geometry along journeys of stages (waypoints, queues, waiting areas, exits) under one of several microscopic operational models, such as the collision-free speed model with rotational steering and the WarpDriver model. It is used to study crowd movement through bottlenecks and corners, lane formation, queues, route choice and the evacuation times of buildings and public spaces. The Civil Safety Research institute (IAS-7) of Forschungszentrum Jülich in Germany started it, first as a C++ command-line application in 2010 and since rewritten as a Python package with a C++ core, and a wider community now contributes. Coverage is any geometry the user supplies, from a corridor to a stadium or station; resolution is the individual pedestrian with time steps of fractions of a second. It is installed from PyPI (version 1.4.2, May 2026), with source on GitHub, documentation and example notebooks, and a Zenodo software DOI. Licence: GNU LGPL v3, free. Caveats: model parameters must be calibrated for a given population and situation, it simulates walking only (no fire or smoke), and references to versions before 0.10 describe the old application. Simulation uses: agent-based evacuation and crowd-management studies for emergency response planning in buildings, transport hubs and events. Related: Aamks couples evacuation with fire simulation (catalogued as platform-aamks), and the Jülich pedestrian data archive in the register supplies experiments for calibration.
